commands.name: select
commands.why: SELECT the application. Nothing else answers before it.

commands.name: verify_pin
commands.why: VERIFY PIN, ASCII in the data field. Both the normal and the duress PIN answer 0x9000; nothing about the response says which.

commands.name: unblock
commands.why: UNBLOCK with the PUK after the retry counter reaches zero.

commands.name: get_card_object
commands.why: Identified mode: the whole signed card object. Needs a verified PIN, because the reader learns a stable credential reference.

commands.name: sign_challenge
commands.why: Key mode: data is scope_len(1) || scope || challenge.

note: Signatures and pairwise handles are NOT pinned here: they depend on keys, and pinning them would pin a key every implementer would need. The command encodings, the status-word protocol and response_body_hex below are the deterministic contract.

response_body.why: What the card signs at presentation. Length-prefixed so no concatenation trick can shift the boundary between challenge and scope.

session.meaning: the application answers with its doc type, version, tries left
the card signs nothing before a PIN
two attempts left; the count is announced
a blocked card refuses the CORRECT PIN too, and refuses BOTH correct PINs identically

status_words.63cX: wrong PIN or PUK; X is the number of attempts remaining
status_words.6982: security status not satisfied (no PIN verified)
status_words.6a80: wrong data (a malformed command, or a challenge under 16 bytes)
